chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara and Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Bureyd ibn Mu'awiya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the woman whose husband is absent from her, when he dies: He (peace be upon him) said: 'The woman widowed from her husband should observe the waiting period from the day the news comes to her, because she mourns over him.'

key_terms.الْغَائِبِ: The absent one (husband who is missing or away)

ai.seo_question: When does the waiting period begin for a widow whose husband died while absent?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the commencement of the iddah for a widow whose husband died in his absence, ruling that the period begins upon the receipt of news rather than the actual date of death. This establishes the principle of 'presence of mind' for mourning obligations, distinguishing it from cases where the death is witnessed. The ruling underscores the practical application of iddah as a period of emotional processing and legal clarity for remarriage.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara and Muhammad Bin Muslim, and Bureyd Bin MUawiya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said regarding the woman whose husband is absent from her, when he dies. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The woman widowed from her husband should observe the waiting period from the day the news comes to her, because she mourns over him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from Zurarah Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Burayd who has said the following: “About the case of a woman whose husband is absent when he dies, abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
She must count her waiting period from the day the news reaches her because she commences mourning for him.’”
